claim_verdicts.evidence: git-merge-base (last updated in 2.43.0, so current for 2.54): "A common ancestor that does not have any better common ancestor is a best common ancestor, i.e. a merge base. Note that there can be more than one merge base for a pair of commits." "Newest" is not the definition and contradicts "more than one". 09c8526 re-checked on Git 2.54.0 in donhang-lab: `git merge-base --all main feature/shipping` prints only 09c8526.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: merge base — a commit both lines of work have that no other shared commit comes after (Git's own name for it is the best common ancestor); a tangled history can have more than one, here there is exactly one, and Git works it out before combining anything. In the playground it is `09c8526`.

claim_verdicts.evidence: git-merge 2.54.0 ("last updated in 2.54.0"): "record the result in a new commit along with the names of the two parent commits". gitglossary 2.54.0, merge: "Unless it is a fast-forward, a successful merge results in creation of a new commit ... with parents being the tips of the merged branches". Parent order not stated in docs; re-run of merge-demo.sh on Git 2.54.0 prints "parents: 57a2d53 59f8ec8" with HEAD on 57a2d53.

git-merge 2.54.0: "No other changes are made." Re-run on Git 2.54.0: after the merge `git log --oneline -2 feature/shipping` prints "59f8ec8 Charge no shipping over two million / 1108382 Add shipping.sh", and the graph shows 57a2d53, c812dbd, b3472f6, 09c8526 under the same ids as before.

git-merge 2.54.0 FAST-FORWARD MERGE: "a new commit is not needed to store the combined history; instead, the HEAD (along with the index) is updated to point at the named commit, without creating an extra merge commit." "--ff is the default unless merging an annotated ... tag". Run on 2.54.0: `git switch -c ff-test 09c8526 && git merge feature/shipping` prints "Updating 09c8526..59f8ec8 / Fast-forward" and creates shipping.sh; no merge.ff config set.

git-rebase 2.54.0 ("last updated in 2.54.0"): "Make a list of all commits on your current branch since it branched off from <upstream> that do not have an equivalent commit in <upstream>." "Replay the commits, one by one, in order." "Update your branch to point to the final commit". The equivalent-commit filter does not apply here. Re-run on 2.54.0: 1108382 -> 826899a, 59f8ec8 -> 415ff6b.

git-gc (last updated in 2.52.0, current for 2.54): "removing unreachable objects"; "--prune=<date> Prune loose objects older than date (default is 2 weeks ago, overridable by the config variable gc.pruneExpire)"; "git gc tries very hard not to delete objects that are referenced anywhere ... remote-tracking branches, reflogs".

git-push (2.54.0 redirects to 2.53.0): "Usually, git push will refuse to update a branch that is not an ancestor of the commit being pushed." --force: "This flag disables that check ... It can cause the remote repository to lose commits". git-rebase 2.54.0: "Rebasing ... a branch that others have based work on is a bad idea: anyone downstream of it is forced to manually fix their history."

git-switch (2.54.0 redirects to 2.51.0): -c: "Create a new branch named <new-branch> starting at <start-point> before switching to the branch." DESCRIPTION: "Switch to a specified branch. The working tree and the index are updated to match the branch."
git-merge 2.54.0 --edit/--no-edit: "The --no-edit option can be used to accept the auto-generated message (this is generally discouraged)."

git-log 2.54.0 PRETTY FORMATS: "%h abbreviated commit hash", "%s subject", "%p abbreviated parent hashes". git-show 2.54.0 -s/--no-patch: "Suppress all output from the diff machinery. Useful for commands like git show that show the patch by default". Space separation: 2.54.0 run prints "parents: 57a2d53 59f8ec8".

git-log 2.54.0 --graph: "Draw a text-based graphical representation of the commit history ... This may cause extra lines to be printed in between commits". Glyphs undocumented; checked by running both scripts on Git 2.54.0: merge graph has "*   d89695a", "|\", three "* |", "|/"; final rebase listing has one "*" per line, no "|". Identical to the lesson apart from trailing spaces.
claim_verdicts.source: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log/2.54.0; merge-demo.sh and rebase-demo.sh run in donhang-lab (git 2.54.0)

claim_verdicts.evidence: Re-run on Git 2.54.0 (docker exec donhang-lab bash /repo/scripts/git/merge-demo.sh; scripts identical at stage-0 and HEAD): "d89695a Merge branch 'feature/shipping' into merge-demo / parents: 57a2d53 59f8ec8", then "59f8ec8 ...", "1108382 ...". Same ids as the lesson. `git cat-file -p 59f8ec8` shows the fixed author "Mai Anh <mai.anh@example.com> 1770519600 +0700".
claim_verdicts.source: examples/don-hang@stage-0 scripts/git/merge-demo.sh, git-playground/build-history.sh; run in donhang-lab

claim_verdicts.evidence: Re-run on Git 2.54.0 (rebase-demo.sh): before "59f8ec8 Charge no shipping over two million / 1108382 Add shipping.sh"; after "415ff6b Charge no shipping over two million / 826899a Add shipping.sh"; final graph eight lines each a single "*" with no "|". Matches the lesson's listing; its "..." cuts are consistent with the full output.

Re-run on Git 2.54.0, first listing line: "* 59f8ec8 (HEAD -> rebase-demo, origin/feature/shipping, feature/shipping) Charge no shipping over two million"; third: "| * 57a2d53 (origin/main, origin/HEAD, main) Add a README". Identical to the lesson.

Behaviour holds on the pinned version: git-merge 2.54.0 ort: "This is the default merge strategy when pulling or merging one branch." Re-run on Git 2.54.0 prints "Merge made by the 'ort' strategy." But the ledger text still names "Git 2.46", no longer the version in content/versions.yaml (git: 2.54). The lesson body names no version, so only the ledger is stale.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Git 2.54 combines the two sides with a named strategy; the captured merge reports `Merge made by the 'ort' strategy.`, ort being the strategy Git chooses by default when merging one branch into the current one.

claim_verdicts.evidence: git-merge 2.54.0: "A merge stops if there's a conflict that cannot be resolved automatically". git-rebase 2.54.0: "Replay the commits, one by one, in order" and "If there is a merge conflict during this process, git rebase will stop at the first problematic commit ... you can continue the rebasing process with git rebase --continue", so each replayed commit can stop again.

Unchanged from round 1: the mechanical halves hold on 2.54.0 (merge graph keeps the fork, rebased listing is one column); prevalence of "a common team rule" has no source in git-scm.com/docs 2.54.0 (git-merge, git-rebase take no position). Opinion, attributed as common practice with no "should"; non-blocking.

git-rebase 2.54.0 RECOVERING FROM UPSTREAM REBASE: "Rebasing (or any other form of rewriting) a branch that others have based work on is a bad idea: anyone downstream of it is forced to manually fix their history." git-merge 2.54.0: "No other changes are made." The claim's condition matches the doc's.

gitglossary 2.54.0 ("last updated in 2.54.0"), object: "uniquely identified by the SHA-1 of its contents. Consequently, an object cannot be changed." commit object: contains "parents, committer, author, date and the tree object". `git cat-file -p 59f8ec8` on 2.54.0 shows a "parent 1108382..." line in the object.

git-log 2.54.0 --decorate: "The option --decorate is short-hand for --decorate=short. Default to configuration value of log.decorate if configured, otherwise, auto." auto: "if the output is going to a terminal, the ref names are shown as if short were given, otherwise no ref names are shown." The claim holds; the prose's exclusivity does not (section 5 issue).

git-rebase 2.54.0: "When starting the rebase, ORIG_HEAD is set to point to the commit at the tip of the to-be-rebased branch." "The previous branch tip, however, is accessible using the reflog of the current branch (i.e. @{1}". git-gc keeps objects referenced by "reflogs".
